Rashi on Chullin 16a:10:1.hebrew: תברא - קשיא הך רישא לסיפא, ותרי תנאי נינהו: מר חשיב ליה תלוש להאי כותל, ומר חשיב ליה מחובר. מר חשיב ליה תלוש, הואיל ולאו מחובר מעיקרו הוא, שכבר היו אבניו תלושות וחברם בבנין, ומר חשיב ליה מחובר, והיינו תנאי דאמר לעיל:
Rashi on Chullin 16a:10:1.english: Broken - [Meaning:] This first clause is difficult in light of the last clause, and they are [the rulings of] two [disputing] Tannaim: one Sage deems this wall detached, and the other Sage deems it attached. One Sage deems it detached, since it was not attached from the outset - for its stones had already been detached and he joined them together in the building - and the other Sage deems it attached; and this is the same dispute of the Tannaim stated above.

Rashi on Chullin 16a:10:2.english: It is one Tanna - And according to all opinions, something that was detached and then reattached is considered detached.

Rashi on Chullin 16a:10:3.hebrew: בכותל מערה - שהוא עשוי מאליו, שחוקק הקרקע, והכותל עומד מאליו ומחובר מעיקרו הוא. אבל בכותל בנין, שהוא תלוש, בשביל שלא ילקה הכותל, דלא ניחא ליה בהו, אינו בכי יותן. אבל בשביל שיודח, דאחשבינהו לצורך כותל, מכשרי זרעים לטומאה:
Rashi on Chullin 16a:10:3.english: In the wall of a cave - Because it is made on its own, in that one dug out the ground, and the wall stands by itself and is attached [to the ground] from its very origin. But in the case of a built wall, which is detached, if [the bowl was placed] so that the wall not be damaged, since he does not desire that [water], it is not [rendered susceptible through the verse] "when water is put." But if [it was placed] so that [the wall] be washed, since he thereby considers [the water] necessary for the wall, it renders the seeds susceptible to impurity.

Rashi on Chullin 16a:1:1.hebrew: קשיין אהדדי - דקתני רישא במחובר לקרקע שחיטתו כשרה, אלמא בדיעבד שפיר דמי, והדר תני היה צור יוצא כו':
Rashi on Chullin 16a:1:1.english: They contradict each other - For the first clause teaches that with regard to [an animal] attached to the ground, its slaughter is valid - proving that after the fact it is fine - and then it teaches, "If a rock was protruding..." etc.

Rashi on Chullin 16a:1:2.hebrew: אלא לאו ש"מ כו' - והא מתניתין רבי היא, דאי רבי חייא אפילו לכתחלה מכשיר:
Rashi on Chullin 16a:1:2.english: Rather, must one not conclude, etc. - This mishna is [in accordance with the view of] Rebbi, for if it were [in accordance with the view of] Rabbi Chiya, he would deem it fit even ab initio.

Rashi on Chullin 16a:2:1.english: The wheel of the potter - A wheel used by potters who work with clay, and they have a mechanism [mochani] by which they turn it when hollowing out the vessel.

Rashi on Chullin 16a:2:2.hebrew: פחרא - חרס, וחבירו בדניאל בחלומו של נבוכדנצר: "חסף די פחר":
Rashi on Chullin 16a:2:2.english: Pachra - Clay [i.e., earthenware]. Its counterpart appears in the book of Daniel, in Nebuchadnezzar's dream: "clay of the potter" (Daniel 2:41).

Rashi on Chullin 16a:2:3.hebrew: סרנא דפחרא - שחיטתו כשרה, שאדם מגלגלו:
Rashi on Chullin 16a:2:3.english: The axle of a potter's wheel - Its slaughter is valid, because a person turns it [by hand].

Rashi on Chullin 16a:3:1.english: Is similar - [Meaning: this slaughter, performed via the water-wheel mechanism,] is invalid, because the water is what turns it, and this slaughter is not done by human force. And we learned below (Chullin 31a): "If [the knife] fell and slaughtered, its slaughter is invalid," as it is written, "And you shall slaughter, and you shall eat" - that which you slaughter, you eat, etc.

Rashi on Chullin 16a:3:2.hebrew: בכח ראשון - מיד כשנטל הדף המעכב את המים והתחיל לגלגל, ובתחלת גלגולו שחט מכח אדם שנטל הדף:
Rashi on Chullin 16a:3:2.english: With the first force - Immediately when he removed the board that was holding back the water and it began to turn, and at the very start of its turning he performed the slaughtering by the force of the person who removed the board.

Rashi on Chullin 16a:3:3.english: With second force - After the water had turned the wheel a first and a second time.

Rashi on Chullin 16a:4:1.english: That he tied him - He bound him.

Rashi on Chullin 16a:4:2.english: That he let a rush of water loose upon him - [Meaning] that he diverted the water to pass over him, and it swept him away.

Rashi on Chullin 16a:4:3.english: Liable - For he actually killed him with that water, and it is indeed his weapon, and it is not [considered mere] indirect causation.

Rashi on Chullin 16a:4:4.hebrew: בכח ראשון - שקשרו סמוך לשפת המים, וכיון שנקב נקב בשפת המים, מיד באו המים לפיו:
Rashi on Chullin 16a:4:4.english: By primary force - [This means] that he tied him close to the edge of the water, and since he breached the water's edge right there, the water immediately reached his mouth.

Rashi on Chullin 16a:4:5.hebrew: אבל בכח שני - שקשרו ברחוק והמים הלכו שם, אע"פ שהוא נקב הנקב והפכו לשם, פטור, דגרמא בעלמא הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 16a:4:5.english: But with a secondary force - [This refers to a case] where he tied [the mechanism] far away and the water went there [flowing on its own]; even though he is the one who bored the hole and diverted it there, he is exempt, for it is merely indirect causation.

Rashi on Chullin 16a:5:1.hebrew: מאי קאמר - היכי יליף טעמא מהכא:
Rashi on Chullin 16a:5:1.english: What is he saying? - How does he derive the reason from here?

Rashi on Chullin 16a:5:2.english: He said to him: The vav that is written, he meant [that it is] on the block - That is to say, [Rabbi Chiya] gave a reason that is not the accurate one, like one who writes a vav on a log: the whole thing is cut apart at intervals because of the log's "teeth," which are formed with groove after groove and are not smooth. Another interpretation: he calls those grooves a "vav." Rabbi Chiya was following his own opinion, that he had validated earlier that slaughter performed on something still attached [to the ground] is valid.

Rashi on Chullin 16a:5:3.english: And the Gemara raises a difficulty: But the verse states it.

Rashi on Chullin 16a:5:4.hebrew: קרא זריזותיה דאברהם קמ"ל - שחש ונזהר שמא לא ימצא צור אפילו מחובר, והביא עמו מאכלת. ל"א: רב לא שמע דבריו של רבי, אלא מקרא שמע יוצא מפיו ולא ידע על מה, ואמר ליה רב לרבי חייא: מאי קאמר רבי? אמר ליה: טעם הביא לשחיטה שנפסלה במחובר ומן המקרא, אבל אינו עיקר. אמר ליה: והא קרא קאמר כו':
Rashi on Chullin 16a:5:4.english: The verse teaches us Abraham's alacrity - [Meaning,] that he was anxious and careful lest he not find [a sharp] rock, even one still attached [to the ground], and so he brought a knife with him. Another version: Rav did not hear this explanation from Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi]; rather, he heard a verse coming from [Rabbi's] mouth and did not know what it referred to. So Rav said to Rabbi Chiya, "What is Rabbi saying?" He said to him: He brought a support for [the ruling] that slaughtering is invalid with an attached [blade], from the verse, but that is not the main reason. He said to him, "But he did say a verse, etc."

Rashi on Chullin 16a:6:1.hebrew: לענין עבודת כוכבים - דקיימא לן (ע"ז דף מה:) שעובד את ההרים אינן נאסרים ההרים בכך, דכתיב "את אלהיהם על ההרים" ולא ההרים אלהיהם, ה"מ הר דמחובר מעיקרו, אבל תלוש ולבסוף חברו ומשחברו עבדו, נאסר משום "לא ידבק בידך":
Rashi on Chullin 16a:6:1.english: With regard to idolatry - For we hold (Avodah Zarah 45b) that one who worships mountains does not thereby render the mountains forbidden, as it is written, "their gods, upon the mountains" (Deuteronomy 12:2), [implying] the mountains are not their gods. This applies to a mountain that was attached [to the ground] from the outset; but [a stone or rock] that was detached and only afterward attached [to the ground], and after attaching it he worshiped it, it becomes forbidden, on account of [the verse] "let nothing that is proscribed stick to your hand" (Deuteronomy 13:18).

Rashi on Chullin 16a:6:2.english: One who bows to his own house - But he cannot render forbidden [the house] of his fellow.

Rashi on Chullin 16a:7:1.hebrew: לענין הכשר זרעים תנאי היא - אי הוי מחובר אי הוה תלוש, דאי אחשבינהו לגשמים בירידתן לצורך שום דבר ואחר כן נפלו פירות לתוכה, אע"פ שלא ידע כשהוכשרו אותן פירות ולא ניחא ליה בההוא הכשר, הוו מוכשרין, דתנן בתחלת מסכת מכשירין (משנה א): כל משקה שתחלתו לרצון, אע"פ שאין סופו לרצון, מכשיר. וה"מ כי אחשבינהו בירידתן לצורך דבר תלוש, אבל אי אחשבינהו לצורך מחובר לא מכשרי, דהכי תניא בת"כ: אשר יבא עליו מים, אין לי אלא מים וכו', יכול אפילו הן בבורות שיחין ומערות יהו מכשירין, ת"ל כלי, אין לי אלא שמלאן בכלי לשתות, מנין לגבל בהן את הטיט ולכבס בהן את הכלים, ת"ל בכל יטמא, אי בכל יטמא יכול אפילו בבורות שיחין ומערות, ת"ל כלי, מה כלי מיוחד שהוא תלוש מן הקרקע אף כל כו', יכול אפילו חישב עליהם שירדו בבורות ושיחין ומערות יהו מכשירין, ת"ל אשר ישתה, אין לי אלא שמלאן לשתיה, מנין שאם חישב עליהן להדיח עצים ואבנים, ת"ל מים כו'. אלמא אחשבינהו לצורך תלוש מכשירין, לצורך מחובר לא מכשירין, אא"כ ניחא ליה בנפילת הפירות לתוכן, דהיינו הדר אחשבינהו לתלוש. והא דאמרינן בפסחים (דף טז.) מחוברין מכשירין, היינו דניחא ליה שיפלו פירות לתוכן, או להושיט ידיו להדיחן כשיוציא הפירות מן המים:
Rashi on Chullin 16a:7:1.english: Regarding the preparation [to receive impurity] of seeds, it is a tannaitic dispute - [whether the water] is considered attached [to the ground] or whether it is considered detached. For if he designated the rainwater, as it was falling, for the sake of some [detached] item, and afterward produce fell into it - even though he did not know when that produce became susceptible [to impurity] and he was not pleased with that particular act of preparation - it would nonetheless become susceptible. For we learned at the beginning of tractate Makhshirin (Mishnah 1): 'Any liquid whose beginning was with [the owner's] approval, even though its end was not with approval, renders [produce] susceptible [to impurity].' And this applies when he designated it, as it was falling, for the sake of a detached item; but if he designated it for the sake of something attached [to the ground], it does not render susceptible. For so it is taught in Torat Kohanim: '[Any food] upon which water shall come' - I would know only of water, etc. One might think that even if it is in pits, trenches, or caves it should render [produce] susceptible; therefore the verse states 'vessel' - I know only that it applies when he filled them in a vessel for drinking. From where do we know [that it applies] if one kneads clay with it or launders garments with it? The verse states 'in whatever it becomes impure.' Now, if [we derive it] from 'in whatever it becomes impure,' one might think that even [water] in pits, trenches, and caves [would apply]; therefore the verse states 'vessel' - just as a vessel is distinct in that it is detached from the ground, so too everything [must be detached], etc. One might think that even if he merely intended for the water to descend into pits, trenches, and caves it should render [produce] susceptible; therefore the verse states 'which he shall drink' - I know only that it applies when he filled them for drinking. From where do we know that it applies if he intended [the water] to rinse wood and stones with it? The verse states 'water,' etc. This shows: if he designated it for the sake of a detached item, it renders susceptible; for the sake of an attached item, it does not render susceptible - unless he is pleased with the produce falling into it, which amounts to his re-designating it for a detached item. And that which we say in Pesachim (16a), 'attached [water] renders susceptible,' means that he is pleased that the produce fall into it, or that he is pleased to reach in his hands to rinse them when he takes the produce out of the water.

Rashi on Chullin 16a:7:2.hebrew: בשביל שתודח - הקערה, הרי הן בכי יותן. אם נפלו אחר כך על הפירות, אפילו לאחר זמן, הוכשרו, דאחשבינהו להנך משקין להדחת קערה, וניחא ליה בהך נפילה, אפילו לא אחשבינהו לצורך הנך פירות, כי יותן קרינא ביה, דניחא ליה בהך נפילה:
Rashi on Chullin 16a:7:2.english: In order that it be washed - [Referring to] the bowl: these [waters that wash it] have the status of "when it is put" [i.e., liquid willingly applied, which renders produce susceptible to impurity]. If they subsequently fell onto the produce, even after some time had passed, the produce becomes susceptible [to impurity], because he regarded these liquids as being for washing the bowl, and he is content with this falling [onto the produce] - even if he did not have in mind that it was for the sake of the produce. It is called "when it is put," since he is content with this falling.

Rashi on Chullin 16a:7:3.hebrew: בשביל שלא ילקה הכותל - ונפלו על הקערה, וממנו לפירות, לא הוכשרו, דלא ניחא ליה בהנך גשמים ובנפילתן:
Rashi on Chullin 16a:7:3.english: So that the wall would not be damaged - [Meaning:] the rain fell on the bowl, and from it onto the fruit - they are not rendered susceptible [to impurity], because he is not pleased with that rain and with its falling.

Rashi on Chullin 16a:8:1.english: This, that the wall should be washed - For example, they [the drops] were falling near the wall, and one placed a bowl there so that it would carry them to the wall.

Rashi on Chullin 16a:9:1.hebrew: אינו בכי יותן - ואע"ג דאחשבינהו לצורך הכותל, חשיבות דמחובר לאו חשיבות הוא, עד דליחשבינהו לצורך דבר תלוש, כדאמרן:
Rashi on Chullin 16a:9:1.english: It is not [governed by the law of] "when water is placed" - Even though he deemed it significant [i.e., desired the water] for the sake of the wall, significance [given] to something attached [to the ground] is not [genuine] significance, until he deems it significant for the sake of something detached, as we have said.

Tosafot on Chullin 16a:10:1.hebrew: אמר רבי אלעזר תברא כו' - לא שייך לשנויי הכא הא בשביל שיודח הכותל נעשה כמי שלא ילקה הכותל, כיון דאין לו לתלות זה בזה, דאין הטעמים שוין: דהא דלא הוי בכי יותן בשביל שיודח היינו משום דחשיב כמחובר, ובשביל שלא ילקה הוי משום דלא ניחא ליה. ולא דמי לנתן הוא ואמרה היא דבפ"ק דקדושין (דף ה:), דמשני התם נעשה כמי שנתנה היא ואמרה היא, דחד טעמא הוא, משום דכתיב (דברים כד) כי יקח איש אשה, ולא שתקח את עצמה. ואם תאמר, דהכא משמע דפליגי תנאי בתלוש ולבסוף חברו לענין הכשר זרעים, ולרב פפא הוי לכ"ע כתלוש, וא"כ מאי קא מבעיא ליה לרב יוסף בפ' המוכר את הבית (ב"ב דף סו: ושם ד"ה בעי) מי גשמים שחשב עליהם להדיח את האיצטרובל, מהו להכשיר בהן את הזרעים? וי"ל, דלרבי אלעזר דאמר תברא למ"ד מחובר, הוי מבעיא ליה, דשמא איצטרובל לא הוי מחובר כמו בית:
Tosafot on Chullin 16a:10:1.english: Rabbi Elazar said, "[It is] a break," etc. - It is not fitting to answer here that since [the intent is] for the wall to be rinsed, it becomes like [the case of intending] that the wall not be damaged, since one cannot make the one dependent on the other, for the reasons are not the same: the reason that [rinsing] is not included in "that it be given" is because it is considered as attached [to the ground], whereas [when the intent is] that it not be damaged, it is because he does not desire [the water]. And this is not comparable to [the case of] "he gave it, and she said it" in the first chapter of Kiddushin (5b), where the Gemara there answers that it becomes like [the case where] she gave it and she said it, for that is a single reason, because it is written (Deuteronomy 24), "When a man takes a wife" - and not that she take herself. And if you should say: here it implies that the Tannaim disagree about [a case of something] detached and afterward attached, regarding the rendering of seeds susceptible [to impurity], whereas according to Rav Pappa it is, according to all opinions, like something detached - if so, what was Rav Yosef's question in the chapter "One who sells a house" (Bava Batra 66b, and there s.v. "בעי"): rainwater which he intended to use to rinse the wine-strainer (itztruvel) - what is [the law] as to whether it renders the seeds susceptible through it? One can say that according to Rabbi Elazar, who said "it is a break" to the one who holds [the wall is considered] attached, this was Rav Yosef's doubt, for perhaps a wine-strainer is not considered attached like a house.

Tosafot on Chullin 16a:4:1.hebrew: אבל בכח שני גרמא בעלמא הוא - ואכפיתה לא מיחייב, דלא מיבעיא היה עומד שם וכפתו במקומו דפטור, אפילו היה סוף מים לבא עליו, דלא רביה רחמנא מצמצם אלא במקום שהתחיל ההיזק כבר, כגון כבש עליו לתוך האש או לתוך המים, כדתנן בהנשרפין (סנהדרין עז. ושם ד"ה סוף). אבל סוף חום לבא וסוף מים לבא פטור, אפילו כפתו במקום אחר והביאו שם, פטור; אע"ג דאם היה סוף מים לבא עליו היה חייב למאן דאמר אשו משום חציו, דמאי שנא מאשו ברוח מצויה, דאין חילוק בין מקרב האש אצל הדבר למקרב הדבר אצל האש, דהא כופף קומתו של חבירו לפני הדליקה שיכולה ולבא ברוח מצויה חייב, כדאמר בריש הכונס (ב"ק נו. ושם ד"ה אילימא). מ"מ הכא פטור, שבשעה שהביאו שם לא היה סוף מים לבא, אי לאו דאשקיל אחר כך; ואמה דאשקיל לא מיחייב בכח שני, ודומה לזרק חץ ותריס בידו, וקדם בעצמו וסילק את התריס, דפטור:
Tosafot on Chullin 16a:4:1.english: But by a secondary force it is a mere indirect cause - And for the tying [alone] he is not liable. For it goes without saying that if he stood there and tied him in his own place, he would be exempt even if the final [wave of] water was about to reach him there — since the Torah did not require exact [immediate coincidence of the harmful force with the act], except in a place where the damage had already begun, such as if he pushed him into the fire or into the water [that was already there], as we learn in [the chapter] "HaNisrafin" (Sanhedrin 77a, and there s.v. "Sof"). But [where] the final heat or the final water is yet to come, he is exempt, even if he tied him in a different place and then brought him there — he is exempt. Even though, had the final water been about to reach him [right there], he would be liable according to the opinion that "his fire is [treated] like his arrows" — for how does this differ from fire [spread] by a normal wind, where there is no distinction between bringing the fire close to the object and bringing the object close to the fire? For behold, one who bends his fellow's body down in front of a blaze that is able to reach him by way of a normal wind is liable, as stated at the beginning of [the chapter] "HaKones" (Bava Kamma 56a, and there s.v. "Ilaima"). Nevertheless, here he is exempt, because at the time he brought him there the final water was not yet coming, unless he [later] removed [the barrier] afterward — and the moment of removing does not render him liable, [since that is only] a secondary force. And this is similar to one who shot an arrow while [the victim] held a shield in his hand, and [the victim] himself then came forward and removed the shield — which is exempt.

Tosafot on Chullin 16a:5:1.hebrew: מנין לשחיטה שהיא בתלוש שנאמר ויקח את המאכלת - ואם תאמר, והא האי קרא בקדשים כתיב, דבפרק התודה (מנחות דף פב: ושם ד"ה ויקח) ובסוף פ' דם חטאת (זבחים דף צז: ושם ד"ה והתם) נפקא לן מהכא דקדשים טעונין כלי. ואומר ר"ת דלענין תלוש גמרינן נמי אחולין, מדכתיב לשחוט את בנו ולא כתיב לשחוט את העולה; אבל כלי לא שייך למילף בחולין, אלא בקדשים, כשאר עבודות דבעו כלי שרת. ומדכתיב ויקח ולא כתיב ויכין, דרשינן תלוש בחולין; ומדכתיב מאכלת ולא כתיב המחתך, דרשינן כלי בקדשים. ואע"ג דהכא דחי רבי חייא, דזריזותיה דאברהם קמ"ל - התם לא שייך למימר הכי:
Tosafot on Chullin 16a:5:1.english: From where [do we know] that slaughter is [performed] with a detached [object], as it is stated: "and he took the knife" - And if you should say: but this verse is written regarding sacred offerings (kodashim), for in Perek HaTodah (Menachot 82b, and there s.v. "va-yikach") and at the end of Perek Dam Chatat (Zevachim 97b, and there s.v. "ve-hatam") we derive from here that kodashim require a vessel (keli). Rabbeinu Tam says that with regard to [the requirement of] a detached [object], we likewise derive it from [the laws of] chullin (non-sacred animals), since it is written "to slaughter his son" and not "to slaughter the burnt-offering"; but [the requirement of] a vessel cannot be derived from chullin, but only from kodashim, like the other sacrificial services, which require sacred vessels (klei shareit). And since it is written "va-yikach" (and he took) and not "va-yakhin" (and he prepared), we derive [the requirement of] a detached [object] with regard to chullin; and since it is written "ma'akhelet" (knife) and not "ha-mechatech" (the cutter), we derive [the requirement of] a vessel with regard to kodashim. And although here [in our sugya] Rabbi Chiyya retracts [his proof, saying] that [the verse] teaches us [only] Avraham's alacrity, there [regarding kodashim] one cannot say the same.

Tosafot on Chullin 16a:6:1.hebrew: לענין עבודת כוכבים הוי תלוש דאמר רב המשתחוה לבית כו' - לא בעי לאתויי הכא פלוגתא דרבי יוסי ורבנן, דפליגי במשתחוה לאילן בפרק כל הצלמים (ע"ז דף מח.), דאפילו רבנן דשרו התם היינו דוקא אילן שנשרש ויוצא מן הקרקע וחשיב כמחובר מעיקרו, ולא דמי לבית. ומתניתין דכל הצלמים (שם דף מז.) דמי שהיה כותלו סמוך לעבודת כוכבים ונפל כו', אבניו ועציו ועפרו מטמאין כשרץ, לא מצי נמי לאתויי, דהתם כשבנאו מתחלה לשם עבודת כוכבים, או השתחוה מקודם לכל אבן ואבן:
Tosafot on Chullin 16a:6:1.english: Regarding idol worship it is considered detached, as Rav said: one who bows to a house, etc. - There was no need to bring here the dispute of Rabbi Yosi and the Rabbis, who disagree about one who bows to a tree, in Perek Kol HaTzelamim (Avodah Zarah 48a), for even the Rabbis who permit there, that is specifically [in the case of] a tree that is rooted and emerges from the ground and is considered attached from the outset, and it is not comparable to a house. And [as for] the Mishnah of Kol HaTzelamim (ibid. 47a), of one whose wall was adjacent to idol worship and it fell, etc., [whose] stones, wood, and earth become impure like a sheretz - that too he could not bring, for there it is a case where he built it from the outset for the sake of idol worship, or he bowed beforehand to each and every stone.
